categories.name: PWM Peripheral, Pin & Electrical Interface
categories.description: Covers the MCU pin assignment, timer alternate-function setup, carrier generation, output electrical constraints, and safe interfacing to external loads.
requirements: The firmware shall output the PWM signal on Arduino D7 (CN9 pin 8, MCU pin PA8).
The firmware shall configure PA8 in a timer alternate-function mode that supports PWM output (e.g., TIM1 Channel 1).
The PWM requirement shall refer to duty cycle on a 3.3 V MCU logic output and shall not imply a variable 5 V supply rail.
The system shall not drive high‑power loads directly from the MCU pin; an external driver stage shall be used for loads exceeding GPIO electrical limits.
The PWM carrier frequency shall remain constant while the duty cycle changes and throughout the ramp.
By default, the PWM frequency shall be 1 kHz unless an application configuration overrides it.
The firmware shall not reconfigure PA8 or its alternate-function selection while PWM generation is active; the pin shall remain bound to the selected timer channel throughout operation.

Duty-cycle updates shall not introduce extra PWM edges; during active operation each carrier period shall contain no more than one rising and one falling transition, except at 0% or 100% where the output is static.

categories.name: PWM Ramp State Machine & Runtime Execution
categories.description: Covers PWM startup and reset behavior, endpoint handling, continuous ramp sequencing, duty-cycle validity, and nonblocking runtime execution.
requirements: The firmware shall start PWM generation automatically after board initialization.
The firmware shall begin each cycle at 0% duty cycle.
The firmware shall repeat the complete 10‑second up/down PWM duty‑cycle cycle continuously until reset or power‑off.
After any reset, the firmware shall restart the PWM sequence from the defined initial state.
During the up‑ramp, the duty cycle shall increase monotonically from 0% to 100%.
During the down‑ramp, the duty cycle shall decrease monotonically from 100% to 0%.

The firmware shall hold PA8 low (0% duty) whenever PWM generation is inactive, including during initialization and after any reset, until the PWM timer is configured and the initial 0% state is established.

The firmware shall clamp computed duty-cycle values to the valid range inclusive of the endpoints so the timer compare value never underflows below 0 or exceeds the auto-reload period, ensuring realizable 0% and 100% duty cycles.

The firmware shall reverse ramp direction immediately at the duty‑cycle endpoints with no intentional hold time: upon reaching 100% the next update shall decrease duty cycle, and upon reaching 0% the next update shall increase duty cycle.
The firmware shall avoid blocking delays that prevent normal firmware execution while updating the PWM duty cycle.

categories.name: PWM Ramp Timing & Profile Configuration
categories.description: Covers ramp durations, waveform shape, duty-cycle endpoints, update pacing, and smoothness of the configured PWM profile.
requirements: The up‑ramp duration from 0% to 100% duty cycle shall be 5.0 seconds.
The down‑ramp duration from 100% to 0% duty cycle shall be 5.0 seconds.
The complete up‑and‑down PWM duty‑cycle cycle duration shall be 10.0 seconds.
The PWM duty‑cycle ramp shape shall be linear.
The PWM duty‑cycle endpoints shall be 0% and 100%.
The firmware should use sufficiently small duty‑cycle increments to create a smooth ramp.
Duty-cycle updates during each ramp shall be paced by a single monotonic timebase with a fixed update interval for the duration of the ramp.
